From c83557859eaa1286330a4d3d2e1ea0c0988c4604 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Will Deacon <will@kernel.org>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2020 20:38:29 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] arm64: kpti: Fix "kpti=off" when KASLR is enabled

Enabling KASLR forces the use of non-global page-table entries for kernel
mappings, as this is a decision that we have to make very early on before
mapping the kernel proper. When used in conjunction with the "kpti=off"
command-line option, it is possible to use non-global kernel mappings but
with the kpti trampoline disabled.

Since commit 09e3c22a86f6 ("arm64: Use a variable to store non-global
mappings decision"), arm64_kernel_unmapped_at_el0() reflects only the use of
non-global mappings and does not take into account whether the kpti
trampoline is enabled. This breaks context switching of the TPIDRRO_EL0
register for 64-bit tasks, where the clearing of the register is deferred to
the ret-to-user code, but it also breaks the ARM SPE PMU driver which
helpfully recommends passing "kpti=off" on the command line!

Report whether or not KPTI is actually enabled in
arm64_kernel_unmapped_at_el0() and check the 'arm64_use_ng_mappings' global
variable directly when determining the protection flags for kernel mappings.

Cc: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>
Reported-by: Hongbo Yao <yaohongbo@huawei.com>
Tested-by: Hongbo Yao <yaohongbo@huawei.com>
Fixes: 09e3c22a86f6 ("arm64: Use a variable to store non-global mappings decision")
Signed-off-by: Will Deacon <will@kernel.org>

diff --git a/arch/arm64/include/asm/pgtable-prot.h b/arch/arm64/include/asm/pgtable-prot.h
index 6f87839f0249..1305e28225fc 100644
--- a/arch/arm64/include/asm/pgtable-prot.h
+++ b/arch/arm64/include/asm/pgtable-prot.h
@@ -23,11 +23,13 @@
 
 #include <asm/pgtable-types.h>
 
+extern bool arm64_use_ng_mappings;
+
 #define _PROT_DEFAULT		(PTE_TYPE_PAGE | PTE_AF | PTE_SHARED)
 #define _PROT_SECT_DEFAULT	(PMD_TYPE_SECT | PMD_SECT_AF | PMD_SECT_S)
 
-#define PTE_MAYBE_NG		(arm64_kernel_unmapped_at_el0() ? PTE_NG : 0)
-#define PMD_MAYBE_NG		(arm64_kernel_unmapped_at_el0() ? PMD_SECT_NG : 0)
+#define PTE_MAYBE_NG		(arm64_use_ng_mappings ? PTE_NG : 0)
+#define PMD_MAYBE_NG		(arm64_use_ng_mappings ? PMD_SECT_NG : 0)
 
 #define PROT_DEFAULT		(_PROT_DEFAULT | PTE_MAYBE_NG)
 #define PROT_SECT_DEFAULT	(_PROT_SECT_DEFAULT | PMD_MAYBE_NG)
-- 
2.25.1



diff --git a/arch/arm64/include/asm/mmu.h b/arch/arm64/include/asm/mmu.h
index e4d862420bb4..d79ce6df9e12 100644
--- a/arch/arm64/include/asm/mmu.h
+++ b/arch/arm64/include/asm/mmu.h
@@ -29,11 +29,9 @@ typedef struct {
  */
 #define ASID(mm)	((mm)->context.id.counter & 0xffff)
 
-extern bool arm64_use_ng_mappings;
-
 static inline bool arm64_kernel_unmapped_at_el0(void)
 {
-	return arm64_use_ng_mappings;
+	return cpus_have_const_cap(ARM64_UNMAP_KERNEL_AT_EL0);
 }
 
 typedef void (*bp_hardening_cb_t)(void);

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/arm64/include/asm/pgtable-prot.h`**
   - Added an external declaration for the variable `arm64_use_ng_mappings`.
   - Modified the definitions of `PTE_MAYBE_NG` and `PMD_MAYBE_NG` to use the `arm64_use_ng_mappings` variable instead of calling the function `arm64_kernel_unmapped_at_el0()`. This change ensures that the protection flags for kernel mappings are determined based on whether non-global mappings are enabled, rather than the state of the KPTI trampoline.

2. **File: `arch/arm64/include/asm/mmu.h`**
   - Removed the external declaration of `arm64_use_ng_mappings`.
   - Updated the `arm64_kernel_unmapped_at_el0()` function to return a constant capability check (`cpus_have_const_cap(ARM64_UNMAP_KERNEL_AT_EL0)`) instead of relying on the `arm64_use_ng_mappings` variable. This change alters the logic for determining if the kernel is unmapped at EL0.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in `pgtable-prot.h` and `mmu.h` are interrelated as they both deal with the handling of non-global mappings in the context of KPTI (Kernel Page Table Isolation). The change in `pgtable-prot.h` to use the `arm64_use_ng_mappings` variable directly allows for a more straightforward determination of protection flags for kernel mappings, while the update in `mmu.h` shifts the logic of `arm64_kernel_unmapped_at_el0()` to a constant capability check, decoupling it from the KPTI state. Together, these changes aim to fix the issue where the KPTI trampoline could be disabled while still using non-global mappings, ensuring proper context switching and functionality of the ARM SPE PMU driver when "kpti=off" is specified.
